title: Supported coefficient charts through one permissible blowup and auxiliary test strings
statement:
Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, $X\hookrightarrow U$ a closed finite-type subscheme of a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme, without a reducedness assumption [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. On an etale neighbourhood of $a\in X$ supply a regular Hilbert coefficient datum of jet bound $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$, with support $N$, vertices $(0,\alpha_i)$, degrees $d_i$, diagram $D$ and quotient supports $\Delta_i$ [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum, def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Suppose the extended Hilbert function is at most $H_D(t)=\#\{\eta\notin D:|\eta|\le t\}$ on this neighbourhood and its equality locus is the coefficient order locus $S\subset N$. Here the extended function at $b$ is $\dim_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(b)[[T]]/(K_b+(T)^{t+1})$, where $K_b$ is the Taylor extension of the actual defining ideal [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Supply finitely many distinct labelled boundary hypersurfaces which, in the datum's straightened coordinates $(W,Z)$, are distinct coefficient-coordinate hyperplanes $W_i=0$ near every point of $S$.
Consider either the identity, or a blowup of a smooth coordinate center $C\subset S$ having normal crossings with that boundary; use strict transform of $X,N$ in this blowup [def-per-adapted-normal-crossings-center, def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-strict-transform]. Follow it by any finite string consisting only of line products and blowups of intersections of two distinct labelled boundary hypersurfaces, with ordinary cartesian pullback of $X,N$, retaining strict transforms of old boundary and appending the new exceptional divisor or line zero section [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation]. Let $r$ count the line products in this string. After an initial etale localization and Zariski shrink around $a$, these transformed regular coefficient charts have the following properties at every prefix, including over points where the coefficient order conditions fail.
In charts meeting the transformed $N$, with straightened coordinates $(W',Z')$, every boundary hypersurface through a point of $N$ is a distinct coordinate hyperplane among the $W'$. The actual Taylor ideal $K'$ is generated by a finite family $f_i'=\sum_\gamma c'_{i\gamma}(W')(Z')^\gamma$. The transported vertices have zero $W'$ components and diagram $D'$ obtained from $D$ by adjoining $r$ free variables, so $H_{D'}=\Lambda^rH_D$, where $\Lambda F(t)=\sum_{j=0}^tF(j)$. At each such point one of the following alternatives holds: either the extended function of the transformed scheme at that point has the persistent rank-excess witness specified below, or the pure transverse forms $A_i(Z')$ of degrees $d_i$ have unique supported homogeneous division for every degree prefix, and $f_i'(0,Z')=A_i(Z')$ modulo higher-degree terms. In the second alternative there are whole-series identities $(Z')^\beta f_i'=\sum_hq_hf_h'$ for every $\beta$, with $q_h$ supported in $\Delta_h$. The block vertex derivatives belong to their accumulated transverse coordinate ideals with invertible transverse Jacobian, and all forbidden derivatives through degree $Q$ belong to those coordinate ideals, exactly as specified in the datum's conditions (4),(5). In the second alternative these are identities and memberships of series, also when the coefficient order conditions fail through positive-order coefficient terms. The first alternative is allowed when lower-degree pure transverse terms are nonzero; such points are not asserted to admit the second alternative. For an admissible chart the generator and coefficient formulas are $f_i'=e^{-d_i}\sigma^*f_i$ and $c'_{i\gamma}=e^{-(d_i-|\gamma|)}\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}$; for line and boundary-intersection charts they are ordinary pullbacks. The exceptional divisions in these generator and coefficient formulas have regular coefficient functions on the transformed coefficient charts. The supported quotients $q_h$ are elements of each centered completed local ring; no regular-section or algebraization assertion about them on a common Zariski open is made.
For every point in the first alternative, and every point of the transformed $X$ outside the transformed $N$, the extended function has a rank-excess witness: there is an integer $q$ such that, writing $v_t=\dim_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(b)[[T]]/(K'_b+(T)^{t+1})$ for the extended function at that point $b$, with $K'_b$ the Taylor extension of the actual defining ideal of the transformed scheme, $v_t\le H_{D'}(t)$ for $t<q$ and $v_q<H_{D'}(q)$. This witness persists under the subsequent coefficient-coordinate boundary substitutions in the string. The charts and identities commute with residue-field extension and with the faithfully flat centered Taylor maps, including nonclosed points. Empty vertex families have $K'=0$ and no transverse variables. Empty transforms are allowed. This statement concerns transported generators, supports, certificates and extended functions; it asserts no regular-sequence conclusion and no retention of the level at the image of a boundary test.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1 §§5.2,6.1–6.3,6.5–6.6, read at https://arxiv.org/html/0905.3580v1; BM2 Chapter III is the construction reference. Agent structural refinement; archival PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this coefficient-chart transport.

proof.text: Work on the supplied chart and on the smooth component of $N$ containing $a$. Its defining equations and the finitely many block Jacobians are units or have the specified zero coefficients at $a$. The Taylor map is injective, so a regular coefficient whose Taylor expansion is zero vanishes as a germ; on the integral component it vanishes identically. Applying this coefficientwise to (4),(5) extends their whole-series memberships to $N$; invert the finitely many Jacobian determinants. Restrict the initial forms at $a$ to $W=0$. Since every vertex has zero $W$ part, the homogeneous extra-variable equivalence gives pure transverse division for each prefix. Invert the finitely many restricted division determinants through the stabilization bound of every prefix. Stabilization now supplies pure homogeneous division in all degrees at every point of $N$. These are finite restrictions independent of the later string.

source.place: BM (7.2)(4)--(5), Lemma 7.7, Theorem 8.1 and proof of Theorem 9.6, pp.278--282

proof.text: At $a$, supported division identifies the actual quotient with the $A=L[[W]]$-module $\prod_{\gamma\notin D}A$: quotient and remainder supports constrain only $Z$, and the division map is $A$-linear. The power-series Noetherian lemma applies to the field $L$. This makes $A$ coherent: the kernel of $A^r\to I$ is finitely generated (induct on $r$, projecting a submodule to its last coordinate ideal), for every finitely generated ideal $I$. A product of flat modules is flat, so the quotient is flat over $A$. Apply coherent formal-generation/flatness spreading. Its etale localization supplies an actual retraction $p:U\to N$ realizing the given straightening; it is obtained from $U\times_{\mathbf A^m_w}N$ with the diagonal section. On one neighbourhood the supplied formal sections generate every actual Taylor ideal, and $X\to N$ is flat. No supported quotient is spread as a regular section.

source.place: Agent E2 repair: actual etale retraction, coherent generation and flatness, using complete normal forms

proof.text: Consider a point $b\in N$ where all lower-degree pure coefficients vanish. Step 1 gives the pure initial forms and prefix division in $L_b[[Z]]$. Divide the fibre ideal $(f_{i,b}(0,Z))$ by this family. If its function is strictly below the transverse diagram, adjoining the coefficient variables and the finite-jet specialization calculation of Step 9 give a persistent strict witness for the actual ideal. Otherwise the field division theorem says that every fibre remainder is zero. The complete-parameter division lemma, with $A=L_b[[W]]$ and the flat quotient supplied by Step 2, then gives supported expansions of every element of the actual ideal, in particular every $Z^\beta f_i$. Its quotients lie in $L_b[[W,Z]]$. Conditions (4),(5) and their Jacobian units hold by Step 1. This proves the second alternative at that point without any total-order assertion there. A nonzero lower pure coefficient is treated by the first-drop calculation of Step 10.

source.place: Agent E2 repair: fibre division followed by complete-parameter flat lifting

proof.text: Prepare the uniform off-support test using finite relative jets of $U\to N$ and regular generators of the actual coherent ideal. For $0\le t\le Q$ put $r_t=\#(D_{\rm tr}\cap\{|\gamma|\le t\})$, where $D_{\rm tr}$ omits the free coefficient variables. Invert one nonzero $r_t$-minor at $a$ for each $t$; rank zero needs no inversion. Apply the relative supported-jet identity in the Taylor ring at $a$. Its right side contains the selected $g_j$, and $(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=(Z)$: write $g=M(W,Z)Z$ and invert $\det M$. Thus the ideal of $N$ is contained, after Taylor expansion, in the sum of the rank-excess minor ideals. Faithful-flat contraction gives this inclusion for coherent stalk ideals; their finite generation extends it to one open $U$. All these are FINITE ideals of relative jet matrices. Their entries are truncated transverse derivatives of regular generators, so coefficient base change fixing $Z$ just substitutes entries. Consequently the pivot units and the inclusion persist under every later coefficient base change, without descent of any infinite supported quotient.

source.place: Agent E2 repair: finite relative determinant ideals, contraction and coefficient base change

proof.text: Use coordinates $W=(T,Y)$ on $N$ with $C=V(Y,Z)$. For $b_{i\gamma}=d_i-|\gamma|>0$, the order inequalities along the smooth reduced $C$ imply $c_{i\gamma}\in(Y)^{b_{i\gamma}}$: all lower normal derivatives restrict to zero on $C$, and the normal Taylor expansion has no monomials of smaller degree. Faithful flatness of the centered Taylor maps contracts this membership to the regular stalk. Thus $f_i\in P^{d_i}$ for $P=(Y,Z)$; at a point of $C\subset S$ its ordinary order is $d_i$, so its $P$-order is exactly $d_i$. The coordinate-blowup division lemma therefore identifies the saturated total ideal with $(e^{-d_i}\sigma^*f_i)_i$. It applies without reducedness of the quotient. Away from $C$ the morphism is an isomorphism, so use actual ideal generation from Step 2 and the finite relative tests of Step 4. Empty strict transforms contribute no points.

source.place: BM Lemma 7.22, Corollary 7.24 and proof of Theorem 9.4, pp.269--271,277--278

proof.text:
In a chart meeting $N'$, choose a coefficient pivot $e=Y_1$, and write $Y_j=e(\eta_j+U_j)$, $Z=eZ'$, $T=T'$. The strict transform is $Z'=0$. Substitution gives
$$f_i'=\sum_\gamma e^{|\gamma|-d_i}\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}(Z')^\gamma.$$
For $|\gamma|<d_i$ Step 5 supplies exactly the exceptional divisibility required; for $|\gamma|\ge d_i$ only nonnegative powers occur. On $N'$ the degree-$d_i$ pure coefficients are the original $c_{i\gamma}$ evaluated at the image. Hence their supported homogeneous division matrices are the same invertible matrices retained in Step 1. The lower pure coefficients may be nonzero, and will be treated separately. There is no division formula at a chart of the identity; its formulas are ordinary pullback.

At the image point in $C\subset S$, divide $Z^\beta f_i$ by the original supported family. Its $P$-order is $d_i+|\beta|$, so the quotient estimate gives
$$Z^\beta f_i=\sum_hq_hf_h,\quad q_h\in P^{\max(0,d_i+|\beta|-d_h)},\quad\operatorname{supp}q_h\subseteq\Delta_h.$$
After substitution and cancellation of $e^{d_i+|\beta|}$ this becomes
$$(Z')^\beta f_i'=\sum_h e^{d_h-d_i-|\beta|}\sigma^*q_h\,f_h'.$$
By that estimate every coefficient on the right is a formal series in the completed local ring at the new point, without exceptional pole; it is not asserted to be a regular function on a Zariski open. Quotient supports constrain only transverse exponents: coefficient variables are unrestricted and $Z=eZ'$ has no translation. Thus the transformed quotients retain exactly their supports. The equalities concern whole series and do not use any order inequality upstairs.

source.place: BM Lemma 7.22 and proof of Theorem 7.20, verification of (3)

proof.text:
For a selected derivative in a degree-$d$ block the chain rule gives $g_j'=e^{-1}\sigma^*g_j$ and $\partial_{Z_k'}g_j'=\sigma^*(\partial_{Z_k}g_j)$. Since $g_j\in(Z^\ell)$ and $Z=eZ'$, $g_j'\in((Z')^\ell)$; its transverse Jacobian is invertible at the new point. For a forbidden derivative,
$$\partial_{(Z')^\ell}^{\delta}f_i'=e^{|\delta|-d_i}\sigma^*(\partial_{Z^\ell}^{\delta}f_i).$$
It belongs to $((Z')^\ell)$ after inverting $e$. The derivative on the left is a regular series. The quotient by $((Z')^\ell)$ is a power-series ring in the remaining variables, and multiplication by $e$ is injective there by coefficient shifting. Cancelling a power of $e$ proves the membership before localization. This proves (4),(5) as whole-series identities even when coefficient order drops.

source.place: BM proof of Theorem 7.20, verification of (4),(5)

proof.text: Here is the finite-jet comparison used for all discarded cases. For an ideal generated by finitely many $h_i(U,V)$, setting coefficient variables $U$ to zero can only increase every jet-quotient dimension. Indeed truncate all monomial multiples of $h_i(\lambda U,V)$ at degree $t$. The resulting finite matrix is polynomial in $\lambda$ and has constant rank for every nonzero $\lambda$, because scaling $U$ is an invertible substitution. Every larger minor vanishes on the infinite field and hence is the zero polynomial. Its specialization at zero therefore has no larger rank. The same calculation applies after any local coefficient substitution fixing $V$: its restriction at the closed coefficient point is the same ideal in $L[[V]]$. In comparing with a diagram with free coefficient variables, the reference restricted ideal must be extended by the same number of free variables.

source.place: BM Lemmas 7.25--7.26; explicit polynomial-minor specialization argument

proof.text: At a point on $N'$ set all coefficient variables to zero and consider the resulting transverse family $p_i(Z')$. If every $p_i$ has no terms below $d_i$, Steps 1 and 6 give precisely its required pure forms $A_i$ and higher terms. Steps 7--8 supply all the stipulated certificates, so this is the second alternative. Otherwise let $m$ be the smallest order of a $p_i$ less than $d_i$, and retain the prefix with $d_h\le m$. No member of that prefix drops. Homogeneous division for it gives independent supported relation columns through degree $m$. Condition (5), with $m<d_i\le Q+1$, makes the degree-$m$ part of a dropping $p_i$ supported outside the prefix diagram: evaluate its forbidden derivatives at the accumulated transverse variables zero and divide by the nonzero factorial. This is one additional independent relation. The omitted vertices have degree $>m$, so the transverse jet dimensions are at most the reference through $m$, and strictly smaller at $m$. Apply Step 9 and adjoin the coefficient variables to get a strict lexicographic witness for the actual ideal.

source.place: BM proof of Theorem 7.20, Case I(b); agent application to the pure transverse restriction

proof.text: For directions off $N'$, take the homogeneous initial forms $H_i(Y,Z)$ at the image point in $C$, over its residue field. They depend only on center variables: $f_i\in(Y,Z)^{d_i}$ and their total order is $d_i$. Their pure top $Z$ parts are $A_i(Z)$. Fix $(\eta,\zeta)$ with $\zeta\ne0$ and put $p_i(V)=H_i(\eta,\zeta+V)$. Some $p_i$ has order $<d_i$: otherwise each selected degree-$(d_i-1)$ transverse derivative would vanish at $V=0$, whereas those derivatives are an invertible constant matrix applied to $\zeta$. In the first dropping degree block, the preceding blocks retain order; their derivative equations force the accumulated preceding components of $\zeta$ to be zero. Their initial forms are the pure $A_h(V)$ and have prefix division. Since the preceding components of $\zeta$ are zero, the forbidden derivative memberships still kill every low-degree monomial in that prefix diagram. The least nonzero part of a dropping $p_i$ is therefore an independent complement-supported relation, exactly as in Step 10. This proves a strict jet witness for $(p_i)$ relative to the transverse diagram, with inequalities at preceding degrees.

source.place: BM (7.27)--(7.30), with an explicit pure-transverse first-dropping-block argument

proof.text: In a coefficient-pivot chart the formulas are $T=S$, $Y_1=e$, $Y_j=e(\eta_j+U_j)$ and $Z=e(\zeta+V)$. Setting all coefficient variables $(S,e,U)$ to zero leaves $p_i(V)=H_i(1,\widetilde\eta,\zeta+V)$. Step 11 gives its strict witness when $\zeta\ne0$, which is exactly the condition for the point to be off $N'$. In a transverse-pivot chart use $T=S$, $Y=eU$, $Z_1=e$, $Z_j=e(\zeta_j+V_j)$ with $\zeta_1=1$. Setting coefficient variables $(S,e,U)$ to zero leaves $p_i(V)=H_i(0,1,\widetilde\zeta+\widetilde V)$, independent of the pivot transverse variable. The omitted free pivot variable is a coefficient variable $e$, so both the reference and the comparison have the same total number of variables. Step 11 applies to the translated transverse polynomial ideal (with its pivot direction nonzero), or equivalently to its dehomogenization times a free variable; the change from centered pivot coordinate $x$ is $Z_1=1+x$, $Z_j=(1+x)(\zeta_j+V_j)$. The factors $(1+x)^{d_i}$ are units. Step 9 transfers the strict comparison to the actual ideal. Only homogeneous polynomials are evaluated at nonzero transverse constants.

source.place: BM (7.28)--(7.30), Theorem 7.20 Cases I and II

proof.text: Every strict case obtained from a pure transverse fibre ideal or from Steps 10--12 is bounded by that restricted ideal. Subsequent local coefficient substitutions leave its closed coefficient fibre unchanged; Step 9 therefore preserves the strict bound. A line sums both functions, preserving the first strict inequality. For the identity, a point outside $N$ has a nonzero relative rank-excess minor by Step 4, while the retained pivot minors give rank at least $r_t$ at every preceding degree. Its relative fibre function is therefore at most the transverse reference through the first excess and strictly below it there. Step 9, with all coefficient variables restored, gives the required extended-function witness. Since the relative matrices, their pivot units and the ideal inclusion base-change, this argument applies after every auxiliary coefficient substitution. In the non-exceptional part of the admissible blowup use its isomorphism with $U\setminus C$; rescaling transverse coordinates by its invertible pivot does not change relative jet ranks. Over $C$, Steps 11--12 give the pure polynomial bounds instead.

source.place: Agent E2 repair: persistence of finite relative tests and pure fibre bounds

proof.text: For an auxiliary intersection use $W_u=e$, $W_v=e(\xi+V)$ and $Z=Z'$. Its inverse-image support is $Z'=0$, and actual defining ideals and coefficients are ordinary pullbacks. Apply the substitution to every certificate: $Z^\beta\sigma(f_i)=\sum_h\sigma(q_h)\sigma(f_h)$. Supports are preserved since they only constrain $Z$. Derivatives in $Z$ commute coefficientwise with substitution and the transverse Jacobian unit stays a unit. The pure transverse restriction is unchanged at a centered point over the old one. The coordinate-subspace chart description shows that the two old boundary hyperplanes become the exceptional hyperplane and one ratio hyperplane; all other labels keep their coordinate equations, with the pivot's strict transform empty. Thus distinct surviving labels and the new exceptional divisor are distinct coefficient hyperplanes. This argument applies to each chart and each next intersection, irrespective of equality of levels.

source.place: BM Theorem 7.21; BMT §5.2 exceptional transformation; explicit coefficient substitution

proof.text: For the initial admissible blowup, the same coordinate-chart calculation includes all center variables $(Y,Z)$. Charts meeting $N'$ have a $Y$ pivot. On $N'$ the surviving old boundary equations are either unscaled parameters or ratios of coefficient parameters, and the new exceptional equation is $e$. The pivot label disappears, and all remaining labels are distinct. The adapted-coordinate hypothesis ensures that these are the complete list of components through the point. At a line product append a free coefficient variable $t$ and its zero hyperplane. Every ideal and certificate pulls back, and $D$ is replaced by $D\times\mathbf N$. Counting monomials of fixed $t$-exponent gives $H_{D\times\mathbf N}(q)=\sum_{j=0}^qH_D(j)$. Induction on the auxiliary string, using Steps 13--14 at its two kinds of successor, gives all assertions at each prefix and $H_{D'}=\Lambda^rH_D$.

For arbitrary scheme points take the residue-field base change at that point and complete at its diagonal rational point. The diagonal Taylor lemma supplies precisely the full ambient-variable ring used here and faithful flatness, without a closed-point assumption. Every displayed coefficient substitution and derivative identity then commutes with coefficient-field extension; each homogeneous division matrix stays invertible. Faithful-flat ideal contraction identifies the computed finite ideals with the actual stalk ideals; the jet-diagram comparison identifies their dimensions with the extended functions and handles the line summations. Thus no argument replaced the extended function by the unsummed local one. If the family is empty, Step 2 makes the actual ideal zero near $a$ and there are no transverse variables. Blowups of the whole component have empty strict transform; all other charts have the zero ideal and the free monomial count. Empty transforms and strings cause no exception.

source.place: BMT §§6.1,6.5--6.6; BM Remark 9.5; diagonal centered Taylor comparison
